controller:
  # Cap concurrent workflows cluster-wide.
  #
  # Without this, nothing throttles submission. On 2026-08-11 two
  # independent pile-ups ran the cluster to a standstill at once: 17
  # openbao test workflows wedged on a nonexistent image, plus seven
  # needle-ci verify pods (1.50 CPU / 4 GiB each) queued behind the
  # three large nodes that are the only ones able to hold them. The
  # scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available and ArgoCD's own sync could
  # not get a pod, so the fix for the bad image could not be applied.
  #
  # 8 is deliberately above steady-state demand — this is a runaway
  # backstop, not a scheduling policy. Excess workflows queue as
  # Pending at the controller instead of stampeding the scheduler.
  parallelism: 8
  workflowDefaults:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: argo-workflow-executor
      # Global wall-clock ceiling for every workflow, including ad-hoc
      # ones submitted by hand or by an agent that forgets to set it.
      #
      # This is the backstop that was missing on 2026-08-11: podGC and
      # ttlStrategy below both only fire AFTER a workflow reaches a
      # terminal state, so a workflow that can never finish is never
      # cleaned up by either. Seventeen openbao workflows sat Running
      # for two days holding CPU/memory reservations because their
      # image (ghcr.io/openbao/openbao:1.15.0) does not exist — the pod
      # could not start, so the workflow could not end, so nothing
      # reclaimed it.
      #
      # One hour is well clear of real work here (rust-verify ~7min,
      # the largest bead-rs benchmark ~8min). A template that genuinely
      # needs longer sets its own higher activeDeadlineSeconds, which
      # overrides this default.
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
      # No default nodeSelector, deliberately.
      #
      # This previously pinned EVERY workflow in the cluster to
      # servers.ngpc.rxt.io/class=ch.vs1.large-iad — the three compute1-8 nodes.
      # That walled the three compute1-4 nodes (4.50 CPU / 7.62 GiB allocatable,
      # half the node count) off from all CI. The large nodes ran at 71-97%
      # committed while a small node sat at 13%.
      #
      # On 2026-08-06 needle-ci spent its entire 2h activeDeadlineSeconds in
      # Pending and never ran a single test: five concurrent kaniko pods
      # (1 CPU / 2Gi each) from one ACB build held all three eligible nodes, and
      # the scheduler had nowhere else to place it. It reported as a deadline
      # breach with no logs.
      #
      # resources.requests already express where a pod can fit: a step needing
      # more than 1.50 CPU / 2.54 GiB will only land on a compute1-8 because no
      # compute1-4 can satisfy the request. Pinning by node class on top of that
      # removes scheduling options without adding safety. A step that genuinely
      # requires a large node should declare its own nodeSelector.
      ttlStrategy:
        secondsAfterCompletion: 3600
        secondsAfterSuccess: 1800
        secondsAfterFailure: 7200
      # Default pod garbage collection
      podGC:
        strategy: OnPodCompletion
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
workflow:
  serviceAccount:
    # false, deliberately: workflow-rbac.yml in this same directory already
    # declares ServiceAccount/argo-workflow together with its Role and
    # RoleBinding, and ArgoCD tracks the live object to argo-workflows-ns-iad-ci
    # (see its argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id). With create:true the chart
    # claimed it too, producing a permanent SharedResourceWarning and marking
    # this Application's sync Failed. Because targetRevision is a static chart
    # version, auto-sync then deduped on revision 1.0.6 and refused to retry —
    # so from 2026-08-02 this app stopped applying ANY values change, including
    # the nodeSelector removal above.
    #
    # Safe to flip: the Helm app is not the tracked owner, so it will not prune
    # the ServiceAccount. The ns app keeps declaring it — no gap.
    create: false
  rbac:
    create: true
crds:
  # install:false, deliberately — this hook is what wedged the Application.
  #
  # Argo's CRDs are too large for Helm's annotation limit, so with
  # install:true the chart ships them as a PreSync hook Job (plus SA /
  # ClusterRole / ClusterRoleBinding hooks) that kubectl-applies them. On
  # this cluster that hook loops forever: the Job runs and Completes in
  # ~45s, the delete policy removes it, ArgoCD returns to "waiting for

command:
KEY_FILE="/vault/userconfig/unseal-key/unseal-key"
while true; do
  TS="[$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)]"
  if [ ! -f "$KEY_FILE" ]; then
    echo "$TS key not mounted, waiting..."
    sleep 30
    continue
  fi
  HEALTH=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/health 2>/dev/null || true)
  SEALED=$(echo "$HEALTH" | grep -o '"sealed":[a-z]*' | cut -d: -f2)
  if [ "$SEALED" = "true" ]; then
    echo "$TS OpenBao sealed — submitting unseal key..."
    KEY=$(cat "$KEY_FILE")
    RESP=$(curl -sf -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/unseal \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d "{\"key\":\"$KEY\"}" 2>&1) || true
    echo "$TS response: ${RESP:-no response}"
  fi
  sleep 10
done
